bib.title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate

question: Does letting an encoder-decoder translator soft-search over source annotations for each target word, instead of compressing the source into one fixed-length vector, improve neural machine translation, especially on long sentences?
hypothesis: A fixed-length context vector is a bottleneck, especially for long sentences; a model that attends to relevant source positions will cope better with long sentences.
contributions: An extension of the encoder-decoder that learns to align and translate jointly, using a bidirectional RNN encoder and a decoder that computes a soft-alignment-weighted context vector per target word.
English-to-French results with a single model comparable to the phrase-based Moses system on sentences with known words.
Qualitative analysis showing the soft-alignments agree with intuition.

method.summary: RNNsearch: a bidirectional gated-RNN encoder produces annotations h_j; at each decoder step an MLP alignment model scores each annotation against the previous decoder state, a softmax gives weights, and the weighted sum is the context vector c_i. Trained jointly with RNNencdec (Cho et al. 2014a) as baseline on WMT'14 En-Fr, with sentence-length caps of 30 and 50 words.

datasets.name: WMT'14 English-French parallel corpora (Europarl, news commentary, UN, two crawled corpora)
datasets.size: 850M words total (Europarl 61M, news commentary 5.5M, UN 421M, crawled 90M and 272.5M); reduced to 348M words
datasets.split: training; sentences up to 30 or 50 words per model
datasets.source: ACL WMT '14 translation task; data selection of Axelrod et al. (2011)
datasets.preprocessing: Moses tokenization script; 30,000-word shortlist per language, others mapped to [UNK]; no lowercasing or stemming

models.name: RNNsearch-30 / RNNsearch-50 / RNNsearch-50*
models.architecture: bidirectional gated-RNN encoder, gated-RNN decoder with additive attention, single maxout hidden layer output
models.layers: inferred: single recurrent layer per direction
models.hidden: 1000 hidden units per RNN (forward, backward, decoder); embedding 620; maxout layer 500; alignment model 1000
models.context: trained on sentences up to 30 (or 50) words

other.RNNsearch-50*: trained much longer until dev performance stopped improving

models.name: RNNencdec-30 / RNNencdec-50
models.architecture: RNN Encoder-Decoder (Cho et al. 2014a), fixed-length context
models.hidden: 1000 hidden units each in encoder and decoder

other.extra_data: uses a separate monolingual corpus of 418M words

training.objective: maximize conditional log-probability of target given source (sentence NLL)
training.steps: Table 2 updates (x10^5): RNNenc-30 8.46, RNNenc-50 6.00, RNNsearch-30 4.71, RNNsearch-50 2.88, RNNsearch-50* 6.67
training.regularisation: gradient L2 norm clipped to threshold 1
training.hardware: NVIDIA TITAN BLACK (-30 models), Quadro K-6000 (-50 models), per Table 2

other.init: recurrent matrices random orthogonal; W_a, U_a Gaussian mean 0 variance 0.001^2; v_a and biases zero; other weights Gaussian mean 0 variance 0.01^2
other.batching: every 20th update fetch 1600 sentence pairs, sort by length, split into 20 minibatches; data shuffled once
other.table2: Columns Updates(x10^5), Epochs, Hours, Train NLL, Dev NLL are in Table 2 but extracted text order is scrambled; not recorded

inference.samples: single model, one translation per sentence; no ensemble

other.unk: models disallowed from generating [UNK] when evaluating on sentences without unknown words

metrics.name: BLEU
metrics.definition: BLEU on news-test-2014; reported on all sentences and on sentences with no unknown word in source or reference

eval.protocol: Single trained model per row; no seeds or significance test reported.

limits: Unknown/rare words are left as an open problem; models trail Moses on all-sentence BLEU (28.45 vs 33.30).
Attention computes weights for every source word for every target word, quadratic cost; authors say this may limit applicability beyond translation (sentences of 15-40 words).
Baseline RNNencdec is Cho et al. (2014a) with 1000 hidden units, not the larger Sutskever LSTM.
Moses uses an extra 418M-word monolingual corpus, so comparison is not like-for-like.
Single run per model, no seeds or significance tests; beam width not given.

terms.definition: concatenation of forward and backward hidden states h_j of the BiRNN for source word x_j
feedforward network a(s_{i-1},h_j) scoring how well inputs around position j and output at position i match

lineage.note: baseline and architecture base; gated hidden unit

lineage.work: Sutskever et al. 2014, Sequence to sequence learning with neural networks

lineage.note: showed basic encoder-decoder deteriorates with sentence length
monotonic Gaussian-mixture alignment; this work allows reordering

code.snippet: c_i = sum_j alpha_ij h_j; alpha_ij = exp(e_ij)/sum_k exp(e_ik); e_ij = a(s_{i-1}, h_j)
a(s_{i-1}, h_j) = v_a^T tanh(W_a s_{i-1} + U_a h_j)
